tracks.title: Ten More Minutes
tracks.subject: a husband who sets the alarm ten minutes before it needs to go off every weekday so he and his wife can lie awake talking about nothing before the day starts
tracks.caption: Gospel-tinged piano folk-pop ballad, mid-2020s chart style. Upright piano playing slow rolling chords, fingerpicked acoustic guitar, a sustained cello line under the verses, a small gospel choir answering the last chorus, soft kick and handclaps on two and four. Intimate room mix with warm tape softness. Male tenor, hushed and close in the verses, opening to full voice in the choruses. 72 BPM, D major. Tender, warm and unhurried. No trap drums, no autotune, no EDM build, no country twang, no rock guitar solo.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - upright piano and cello]

[Verse 1]
Six-fifteen, the phone goes off
I set it early, on purpose
You don't even open your eyes
You just say morning to the pillow

[Chorus]
Give me ten more minutes
Talking nonsense in the dark
Like what we'd name a boat
Before the day knows where we are

[Verse 2]
You tell me what you saw asleep
I swear I was in it too
The heating ticks, the street is dark
Nobody needs us yet

[Chorus]
Give me ten more minutes
Still arguing about the boat
You want Margaret
I say Margaret's a coat

[Bridge - choir enters]
Thirty years from now
I'll still set it early

[Chorus]
Give me ten more minutes
Your cold foot on my shin
Ten more minutes
Then the day can come in

[Outro - piano alone]
Six-fifteen
Stay there, love

tracks.title: Wrong Room, Right Boots
tracks.subject: a woman who walks into the wrong room at the leisure centre expecting spin class and finds a Thursday line-dancing class for pensioners, stays out of politeness, and by week three owns the boots
tracks.caption: 80s-flavoured cowgirl synth-pop, mid-2020s chart style. Gated LinnDrum kit with a driving four-on-the-floor, pulsing analog synth bass, bright stabbing synth brass, a twangy clean electric guitar playing country licks, stacked handclaps. Glossy 80s reverb, punchy wide mix. Female mezzo, sassy half-spoken verses and a big belted chorus. 122 BPM, A major. Cheeky, bright and danceable. No trap hi-hats, no autotune, no dubstep drop, no banjo, no ballad slowdown.

[Intro - synth brass and LinnDrum]

[Verse 1]
Thursday night in cycling shorts
Room four, I thought it said

And Derek in a hat instead

But Joan already said hello

[Chorus]
Wrong room, right boots
Heel, toe, turn around
I came here to sweat

[Verse 2]
Week two, a western shirt
Week three, the boots were red
Joan says I kick too high
Derek nods his head

[Chorus]
Wrong room, right boots
Heel, toe, turn around
Spin class down the hall
Can keep its bikes, I'm country now

[Bridge - handclaps]
Grapevine left
Grapevine right

[Chorus]
Wrong room, right boots
Joan still runs this town
I came here to sweat
Now I'm teaching Derek how

[Outro - twangy guitar and synth bass]
Room four, Thursday night

tracks.title: Name on the Hummus
tracks.subject: a woman whose new flatmate writes his name on everything he puts in the shared fridge, so she starts labelling things back, until she sticks a label with her own name on his forehead and he laughs for the first time
tracks.caption: 70s Laurel Canyon soft-rock pop with a modern pop polish. Warm acoustic piano playing bouncy chords, a clean Telecaster with light chorus picking sunny fills, a round melodic bass, a dry 70s drum kit with tight snare, tambourine on the off-beats, a short flute fill between lines. Dry warm tape sound. Female soprano, breezy and deadpan, close stacked harmonies on the hook. 104 BPM, G major. Sly, sunny and petty. No trap drums, no autotune, no EDM synths, no heavy distortion, no country twang.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - piano and flute]

[Verse 1]
New flatmate moved in Sunday
By Monday there were stickers
Kevin on the yoghurt
Kevin on the butter

[Chorus]
Name on the hummus
Name on the cheese
Fine, Kevin
I bought stickers too, you'll see

[Verse 2]
Now the oven door says Becky
So do the ice tray and the bread
He wrote Kevin on the ketchup
I wrote Becky on his bed

[Chorus]
Name on the hummus
Name on the keys
Name on the light switch
Name on the TV

[Bridge - just piano and tambourine]
Then I stuck one on his forehead
And he laughed out loud
First time I'd heard it

[Chorus]
Name on the hummus
Name on the tea
Now the fridge door says
Kevin and me

[Outro - flute and Telecaster]
Fine, Kev, have the yoghurt

tracks.title: Where's Bernard
tracks.subject: a man whose pet tortoise Bernard escapes into the back garden and stays missing for three weeks while the whole family searches, until he finds him asleep inside his own wellington boot by the back door
tracks.caption: Appalachian old-time string band, porch-session revival style. Old-time fiddle sawing a driving reel with double stops, clawhammer banjo in open tuning, flatpicked acoustic guitar boom-chuck rhythm, upright bass on root and fifth, foot stomps on the beat. One-room live recording with mic bleed, raw and unpolished. Male baritone, plain folk delivery, rough group gang vocals on the chorus. 118 BPM, D major. Rollicking, comic and fond. No drum kit, no electric guitar, no autotune, no pop production, no bluegrass speed-picking showcase.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - fiddle and banjo]

[Verse 1]
Bernard took a walk one Tuesday
Slow as Sunday, out the gate
Ninety years he's got to live
So he's in no hurry, mate

[Chorus]
Where's Bernard, where'd he go
Not in the hedge, not in the peas
Lettuce on a saucer by the door
Where's Bernard, where's he gone

[Verse 2]
The kids put posters on the fence
My wife looked in the shed
We turned the compost twenty times
I looked under the bed

[Chorus]
Where's Bernard, where'd he go
Not by the bins, not in the rhubarb
Three weeks now and the lettuce is limp
Where's Bernard, where's he gone

[Bridge - fiddle break]
Then I went to pull my boots on
And my left boot wouldn't go

[Chorus]
There's Bernard, there he is
Snoring in my wellie
Three weeks by the back door
There's Bernard, home all along

[Outro - stomps and fiddle]
Slow as Sunday, Bernard

tracks.title: Glitter Till Wednesday
tracks.subject: a woman who goes to one Saturday warehouse rave in a glitter top and keeps finding the glitter all through the working week, on her keyboard, in her porridge and on her manager's sleeve during Wednesday's budget meeting
tracks.caption: Sleazepop, 2025-26 underground electronic pop style. Distorted 909 kick on four, a rubbery squelching acid 303 bassline, glassy detuned supersaw stabs, crunchy breakbeat fills between sections, a heavy sub bass. Lo-fi club grit with an overdriven mix bus and a dry close vocal. Female alto, deadpan talk-sung verses, breathy then shouted hook. 132 BPM, F minor. Giddy, cheeky and hot-blooded. No trap drums, no autotune warble, no acoustic guitar, no big pop ballad chorus, no festival EDM drop.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - acid bassline and 909 kick]

[Verse 1]
Saturday, a warehouse in Hackney
Silver top, a size too small
Danced till the lights came on
Washed my hair, no use at all

[Chorus]
Glitter till Wednesday
On my keys, on my phone
Monday at my desk
In the space bar, made a home

[Verse 2]
Tuesday it's in my porridge
Tuesday it's in my tea
Wednesday budget meeting
It's on Gary, next to me

[Pre-Chorus]
He looks down at his sleeve
I look at the floor

[Chorus]
Glitter till Wednesday
On my keys, on his arm
Gary asks me where I've been
I say nowhere, stay calm

[Bridge - breakbeat]
Friday, it's nearly gone
Saturday, top back on

[Outro - acid bassline]
Glitter till Wednesday
See you Saturday

tracks.subject: a student in Yogyakarta whose kos landlady keeps a goose that guards the gate and chases him every night he comes home after ten, so he learns to dodge it in a shoulder-shaking dance
tracks.caption: Indonesian breakbeat kejut bahu (BKB), bar-floor breakbeat style. Chopped amen-style breakbeat drums with snappy snare rolls, rubbery saw bass bouncing on offbeats, short detuned stab synth chords, rave hoover sweeps into each drop. Loud compressed club mix, wide stereo. Cheeky male mid-register vocal, half shouted, half sung, rhythmic and playful. 148 BPM, A minor. Mood of a silly late-night chase turned into a dance. No trap hi-hats, no autotune, no dangdut kendang, no EDM supersaw build, no slow ballad section.

Bawa roti buat sogokan

tracks.title: 餐桌上的火車
tracks.subject: a woman whose boyfriend's model railway slowly takes over their dining table track by track, until they eat dinner on the sofa and the little train delivers the soy sauce
tracks.caption: Mandarin bluegrass, traditional string-band style. Female alto lead with close male harmony on choruses, bright and conversational. 132 BPM, G major. Cheerful, rollicking and teasing. No drum kit, no electric guitar, no pop synths, no autotune, no country-pop polish.

[Intro - banjo roll, fiddle kickoff]

[Verse 1]
你說只放一小段
鐵軌就從盤子旁邊過
第二週多了一座橋
第三週多了車站

我的碗被擠到邊邊
你說那是月台

[Chorus]
餐桌上的火車 嘟嘟嘟

你還在幫它鋪軌

說請注意月台間隙

[Chorus]
餐桌上的火車 嘟嘟嘟
這班專門送醬油
沙發其實也不錯
只要火車準時來

[Outro - banjo and fiddle trade licks]

tracks.title: 阿麥
tracks.subject: a woman in a Taipei studio flat who keeps a sourdough starter named 阿麥 alive, feeding it flour at seven every morning before work and taking the jar with her on the train when she visits a friend for the weekend
tracks.caption: Mandarin nu-jazz broken beat, West London style. Syncopated broken-beat drums with ghost-note snares, warm Fender Rhodes chords, walking upright bass, muted trumpet answering lines, soft synth pads. Dry close drums, soft tape saturation, warm low end. Female mezzo, intimate half-spoken verses, airy chorus. 104 BPM, E♭ minor. Calm, wry and quietly attentive. No trap beats, no EDM drop, no autotune, no rock guitar, no orchestral strings.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - broken-beat drums, Rhodes, muted trumpet]

[Verse 1]
七點鐘 鬧鐘還沒響
我先打開那個玻璃罐
一匙麵粉 一點溫水
阿麥冒了兩個泡

[Pre-Chorus]
它不會說話
但它會長高

[Chorus]
阿麥 阿麥 早安
今天也要吃飽
我去上班你在家
晚上看你多高

[Verse 2]
週末去台中找朋友
罐子放在背包最上面
火車晃了一路
我一直怕它溢出來

[Pre-Chorus]
朋友說妳帶了誰
我說一個室友

[Chorus]
阿麥 阿麥 到了
這裡的水不一樣
你在窗台上發脾氣
明天就帶你回家

[Outro - trumpet over Rhodes, drums thin out]

[Verse 1]
開學前一個晚上
新課本堆成一座山
書套一張一張攤開
我用尺慢慢推

[Pre-Chorus]
推好了這邊
那邊又鼓起來

[Chorus]
包書套 包書套
每本都有小泡泡
推不平就不推了
我幫它們取名字

[Verse 2]
國語課本上是阿胖
數學課本上是小圓
自然課本有三個
叫大哥二哥三哥

[Pre-Chorus]
同學的書平平的
沒有一個有名字

[Chorus]
包書套 包書套
我的書有一家人
老師問這是什麼
我說他們來上學

[Outro - clarinet run, horns, crackle fades]
